[[File:SWCCG Grand Moff Tarkin T-shirt layout encyc.png|thumb|right|260px|Grand Moff Tarkin card T-shirt, for tournament directors only.<ref name="enc188" />]]
'''SWCCG memorabilia''' is the apparel, prizes and promotional material made around the ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game, apart from the cards and their packaging. From 1996 to 2001 [[Decipher]] gave tournament players and directors card T-shirts, pins, patches, medals, bags, binders and trophies. It also sent posters and sales sheets to stores and mailed holiday cards to staff and close associates. It issued tournament-organizer kits and made about 250 Executive Gift Sets for Lucasfilm and Decipher executives.<ref name="enc188" /><ref name="enc190" /><ref name="enc109" /><ref name="talaga-weird" /> Since 2002 the [[Players Committee]] has awarded its own trophies, pins, uncut sheets and other prizes. After the license ended, leftover Decipher stock reached the Players Committee, retailers and third-party repacks.<ref name="tfn-donation" /><ref name="talaga-weird" />

== Apparel ==
=== Card T-shirts ===
Decipher card T-shirts were tournament prizes from 1996. Each showed a card on the front and the SWCCG logo on the sleeve; the back read "Never Underestimate the Power of the Force". Most were white cotton in XL.<ref name="enc188" /><ref name="swca" /> At sanctioned events, the first prize was one of these shirts. Tournament directors received a [[Grand Moff Tarkin]] shirt as a thank-you for running events.<ref name="swca" />

=== Squadron and team shirts ===
[[File:Jim Colson Gold 5 shirt embroidery.jpg|thumb|right|220px|[[Jim Colson]] Gold 5 Squadron Member shirt. Still: [[BoardMatt]].<ref name="colson-gold5" />]]
About 90 elite tournament directors in Decipher's Rebel Squadron received black golf shirts embroidered with their squadron (Gold or Red) and Squadron number. After the 1996 season Decipher sent them "Tour of Duty" patches to add to the shirts.<ref name="swca" /> [[Jim Colson]]'s Gold 5 shirt is a black polo embroidered GOLD 5, with a Rebel Alliance roundel and STAR WARS CCG GOLD SQUAD.<ref name="colson-gold5" />

Players also made their own team shirts. [[Marty Terwilliger]] printed red shirts with "Team Albany" on the front for [[Team Albany]] at DecipherCon 2000.<ref name="sokol-dt" /> Alan Rimmel made [[Team OK-UK]] shirts whose back read "DecipherCon 2k - Came to drink."<ref name="tennet" />

=== Caps ===
A Decipher Customizable Card Group cap is embroidered "DECIPHER CUSTOMIZABLE CARD GROUP" on the front and "THE ART OF GREAT GAMES®" on the back.<ref name="fb-kanner-cap" />

== Holiday cards ==
[[File:Decipher 1997 Christmas card fold-out encyc.jpg|thumb|right|220px|1997 Decipher Christmas card fold-out.<ref name="enc169" /><ref name="talaga-weird" />]]
Decipher mailed Christmas cards to staff and close associates. The 1997 card folds out as a tree of cards. Its printed line reads "On the twelfth day of Christmas Decipher sent to me," and its verses include "Ten Banthas marching."<ref name="enc169" /><ref name="talaga-weird" /> A later card (1998 or 1999) is a staff group photograph with a name legend on the back; signed copies exist. People on that photograph include [[Warren Holland]], [[Chuck Kallenbach]], [[Jerry Darcy]], [[Rob Burns]] and Rick Edelman.<ref name="talaga-weird" />

== Lucasfilm and executive items ==
[[File:SWCCG Executive Gift Set box encyc.png|thumb|right|240px|Executive Gift Set box.<ref name="enc109" />]]
The '''Executive Gift Set''' (2001) was made as a gift for Lucasfilm and Decipher executives. Decipher produced about 250. Each white box with a black top carries the SWCCG logo and "Decipher – The Art of Great Games" embossed in gold. It holds a cut set of [[Premiere Limited]] in reverse sheet order (almost two complete sets) and an Unlimited starter rulebook, with no unique cards. Most were never given out, and they reached the secondary market after Decipher lost the license.<ref name="enc109" /> According to [[Andy Talaga]], the first copies went out unsealed at a Christmas party in 1997 or 1998. He says the sets were never factory-sealed, and Wild Things Games of Salem, Oregon, resealed leftover stock. He describes a production-ratio cut (1× R1, 2× R2, U1/U2, C1/C2/C3 Stormtrooper and Rebel Trooper) plus a rulebook and filler.<ref name="talaga-weird" />

Decipher made a special promotional card to show Lucasfilm, the Location [[Playtest cards#Skywalker Ranch|•Skywalker Ranch]]. It is not a playtest card.<ref name="bisco20261021" /> Its game text reads "If you occupy, Decipher gets the CCG license here."<ref name="encyc3" /> Decipher's July 2000 presentation to Lucasfilm proposed World Championship prizes and George Lucas signature cards.<ref name="pres2000" />

== Tournament prizes ==
=== Decipher era ===
At the [[1996 Decipher World Championship]], regional champions received large glass trophies, the 12 finalists received trophies bearing the Rebel logo, and the World Champion received a large silver platter.<ref name="swca" /> The grand prize was a trip to the Tunisian filming locations of Tatooine. [[Raphael Asselin]] and his tournament director Francis Lalumiere left on 1 May 1997, led by David West Reynolds.<ref name="journey" /> [[Philipp Jacobs]], the 1997 champion, won a 10-day trip to Washington, Las Vegas and Los Angeles.<ref name="jacobs" /> His fellow 1997 finalists received embroidered World Championship Finalist prizes.<ref name="ars" />

Early tournaments gave away free tin tab pins, one Rebel and one Imperial. Other prizes included a "Tournament Player" keychain reading "A Force to Be Reckoned With", Pre-Release Player badges, binders, bags, plates, glass trophies, medals and patches. One bag was made to hold an Anthology box.<ref name="enc190" /> A 2×3 in. "Ask Me About Star Wars CCG" badge (1995) was worn by Decipher or retail representatives.<ref name="swca-badge" /> Rebel Squadron directors received black backpacks embroidered with their squadron, two boxes of each expansion on release, and a pewter medal with the Rebel logo.<ref name="swca" /> A glass [[1999 Decipher World Championship]] trophy is etched "1999 WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP".<ref name="fb-bordier-trophy" /> A tournament poker chip carries a gold emblem.<ref name="enc190" /> Level 1 events used an "A Moment of Triumph" first-place certificate.<ref name="swca-91371" />

The [[1998 Decipher World Championship]] was held on 20–22 November 1998 at the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach. Its grand prize was an all-expense-paid trip and VIP pass to Star Wars Celebration at the Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum in Denver, 30 April–2 May. Each of the 56 players received a complete set of [[Special Edition]]. [[Matt Potter]] won; a trophy case stood in the hotel, and the champion received a medal from Carol Wisely, Decipher's vice-president of marketing, and a handshake from [[Warren Holland]].<ref name="insider-1998" />

For 2000, Decipher replaced its state, provincial and national trophies with more than 500 trophy binders: custom four-pocket binders, each foil-stamped with the event and "Champion" or "Runner-up".<ref name="tfn-binders" /> State Champions received their [[Promotional Foils|promotional foils]] in the binder.<ref name="enc34" /> Decipher also awarded plaques. [[Paul Todd Feldman]] kept a 1999 Decipher Champ plaque from the [[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]].<ref name="drtorch" /> The [[2000 Decipher World Championship]] winner received a World Champion plaque.

=== Players Committee era ===
In April 2002 Decipher donated more than $1 million in product and promotional material to the Players Committee for prize support. It included over 100 variations of uncut sheets and sets of nearly every promotional foil.<ref name="tfn-donation" /> [[Angelo Consoli]] won $5,000 and a trophy at the [[2002 World Championship]].<ref name="tfn-2002" />

The [[2023 Retro League]] awarded a Premiere Dark Side rare uncut sheet and snap pins.<ref name="pc2023" /><ref name="t82155" /> The [[2023 Beezer Bowl]] gave original paintings.<ref name="beezer" /> The reigning Ohio State Champion holds the "King of Ohio" title belt.<ref name="ohio" />

== Tournament kits and store stickers ==
Decipher issued a tournament organizer kit (April 1996 Release). It held an Organizer's Guide, a Tournament Rule Systems booklet, a tournament binder, a "Decipher tournament organizer V.01" CD-ROM, a Command Card scoresheet and a Tournament Sheet.<ref name="pp-misc" /><ref name="pp-kit" /> Some kits included a xerox of the 1 May 1996 FAQ.<ref name="pp-faq" /> The kit was also issued as a sealed packet.<ref name="pp-packet" /> The Command Card is the event scoresheet; see [[Tournaments]]. Stores received a reversed window sticker reading "Sold Here!" for the shop glass, and a gold "STAR WARS CUSTOMIZABLE CARD GAME TOURNAMENT" sticker.<ref name="pp-misc" /><ref name="pp-window" /><ref name="talaga-weird" />

== Deck boxes ==
In 1996 Decipher made empty character deck boxes, 4×4×3 in., with Luke Skywalker, Boba Fett, C-3PO, Leia Organa and Jabba the Hutt. These are smaller than the 300-card [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] boxes of 1998.<ref name="nk-deckbox" /> The Star Wars Collectors Archive also lists a Premiere Darth Vader tournament deck box and Jabba's Palace tournament deck boxes, including Salacious Crumb.<ref name="swca-vader-box" /><ref name="swca-90774" />

== Posters and retail material ==
[[File:Premiere-Limited-expand-the-empire-poster.png|thumb|right|200px|Premiere store poster.<ref name="enc143" />]]
Decipher made a four-panel poster (about 32″ × 10.5″) for every expansion from [[Premiere Limited|Premiere]] through [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]]. The Premiere poster's back is blank; the others carry the expansion's card list, and Death Star II's adds a pre-constructed deck.<ref name="enc134" /> Each set hub shows its poster. Folded copies were mailed to stores; rolled copies were given at conventions. Special Edition exists only folded.<ref name="talaga-weird" />

Larger store posters followed:<ref name="enc143" />
* 27.5″ × 20.5″: Premiere, [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]], [[Special Edition]], [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]]
* 33″ × 25.5″: [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]], [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]]
* 17″ × 22″: Rebel Leader packs
* 16″ × 11″: [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] events
''Science Fiction Age'' (September 1996) included a smaller A New Hope poster.<ref name="enc183" />

Retailers received a sales sheet previewing each new expansion.<ref name="enc110" /> From [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] onward every expansion, revised set, [[Enhanced Premiere]], [[Enhanced Cloud City]], anthology and [[Official Tournament Sealed Deck]] used this sell-sheet format, with MSRP, product number, UPC, ISBN and pack contents. According to [[Andy Talaga]], the Dagobah Limited and Cloud City Limited sheets were printed mainly for staff at trade shows, and fewer than five of each are known. From [[Jabba's Palace Limited|Jabba's Palace]] on, he says, the sheets were compiled into distributor binders.<ref name="talaga-weird" />

[[File:Decipher Premiere clip art ad sheet encyc.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Premiere clip-art ad illustrations sheet.<ref name="enc169" />]]
Decipher also issued a Premiere "CLIP ART AD ILLUSTRATIONS" sheet of black-and-white starter, booster and logo art for retailer ads.<ref name="enc169" /> A 1998 catalog kit held SWCCG material, a CD-ROM demo and flyers in a folder.<ref name="swca-15286" />

Decipher's ads ran in ''Scrye'', ''InQuest'' and ''Star Wars Insider'', in comics and in mailings to distributors and customers. In 1996 an ad for the Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game was packed with Kenner/Hasbro ''Star Wars'' toys.<ref name="enc165" />

== Pre-release pamphlet ==
[[File:Experience the Force pamphlet 1995.jpg|thumb|right|280px|''Experience the Force'' pamphlet, 1995. Still: [[BoardMatt]].<ref name="talaga-weird" />]]
''Experience the Force'' is a pre-launch pamphlet from summer 1995. The back names a first release of December 1995 and shows Luke's Speeder and a Stormtrooper. The interior describes a 324-card Premiere set, printed by Cartamundi of Belgium on heavy card stock with black-foil gold logos.<ref name="talaga-weird" />

== Magazine inserts ==
[[File:InQuest 38 Force Playmat encyc.png|thumb|right|200px|''InQuest'' 38 Force Playmat.<ref name="enc183" />]]
''InQuest'' 38 (June 1998) came with a paper "Force Playmat" that cut in half into a Dark Side mat (Darth Vader's Meditation Chamber) and a Light Side mat (Yoda's Hut). ''Scrye'' included a 40-page players guide with game text for Premiere through Dagobah (August 1997). In January 1998 it added a booklet of the A New Hope through Cloud City rules supplements.<ref name="enc183" /> Oversized card inserts are on [[Oversized cards]].

== Convention items ==
Besides the DecipherCon shirts, DecipherCon 2000 pre-registrants received a foil [[Corellian Corvette]] or [[Imperial-Class Star Destroyer]].<ref name="enc34" /> At conventions, customers who spent more than $20 at the Decipher Store received a 5″ × 7″ oversized card.<ref name="enc108" /> Guests such as [[Shannon Baksa]] and [[Michonne Bourriague]] signed cards at DecipherCon (see [[Oversized cards]]).

Decipher hung oversized card images with velcro tabs on booth walls at Gen Con, Origins and the GAMA trade show. Surviving pieces include a roughly 2 ft × 2 ft [[Collision]] and an oversized [[Chewbacca]] that came from [[Jim Colson]].<ref name="talaga-weird" /> Colson kept vinyl velcro copies of a [[Death Star]] system card and Chewbacca from those walls.<ref name="colson-velcro" /> He also kept a Special Edition vinyl booth card of a Dark Side capital starship.<ref name="colson-se-vinyl" /> A Rebel Leader tournament business card for Kendrick Summers has an order of battle on the back.<ref name="swca-15287" />

== Production proofs ==
Cartamundi printed proof sheets on thin vinyl-like stock (half a card, front only) and mailed them to Decipher in Norfolk for mark-up. An A New Hope locations proof sheet reached collectors with the giant Collision, from a former Decipher vice president of marketing.<ref name="talaga-weird" /> See [[Playtest cards]].

== Leftover stock ==
After [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license|the license ended]] on 31 December 2001, leftover Decipher inventory left Norfolk besides the April 2002 Players Committee donation. Wild Things Games of Salem, Oregon, acquired Decipher's replacement-card backstock: trays of every card, including Alternate Images, foils and ultra rares, plus uncut sheets.<ref name="talaga-weird" /> Uncut sheets are on [[Aftermarket and collecting]]. Hills Wholesale sold leftover sealed product.<ref name="talaga-weird" /> It still lists leftover factory trays of commons.<ref name="hills-tray" /> Third parties bundled leftover packs into mass-market window boxes; see [[Unofficial repackaged products]]. [[Jim Colson]] visited Norfolk as a Players Committee representative while the offices were cleared. He found a pile of playtest cards, miscuts and rejects, and took a few boxes for the committee.<ref name="colson-norfolk" />

[[File:Delaminated SWCCG card metal layer Colson.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Delaminated card metal layer. Still: [[BoardMatt]].<ref name="colson-delam" />]]
Colson showed a delaminated card whose metal layer had separated from the stock.<ref name="colson-delam" />

== Unreleased relics ==
Before the license ended, Decipher consulted Colson about relic cards containing cut film cells, and it had discussed selling factory-graded cards. Neither shipped.<ref name="colson-relics" /> See [[Unreleased cards]].
